thread:
maria (PM): Quick sync — we need a lightweight gating spec for new catalog entries that surfaces clear migration costs to customers. goal: reduce surprise during deprecations and make pin requests explicit.

ashok (Eng): +1. proposed minimal gates: perf bench, quantization compatibility, and rolling-upgrade test. also need a way to indicate 'experimental' vs 'production-ready' in catalog metadata.

liz (ML): For benches I suggest two reps: an end-to-end request latency bench (p50/p99) and a regression harness on a small curated eval set. keep the eval set <100 prompts per model to be fast.

ashok (Eng): Agree. Draft numbers: p99 delta <= 20ms vs baseline for same-seq workloads, and model quality regressions < 2% on the eval set. Thoughts?

maria (PM): Those thresholds seem reasonable for most customers. We should also add a cost-payoff metric: inference cost per 1k tokens change <= 1.3x baseline to consider default pining removal.

jen (Sales): From enterprise calls, customers will accept small perf deltas if we provide clear migration tooling and a 30-day transition window. they also want a flag to opt into pinned-old-model for a fee.

ashok (Eng): Implementation ideas: catalog entry carries fields: `status` (experimental|stable|deprecated), `compat_layers` (boolean), `pin_policy` (auto|manual|paid). runtime will read these and allow pin enforcement during routing. Example fragment:```json
{
  "model": "xyz-13b",
  "status": "stable",
  "pin_policy": "manual",
  "compat_layers": true
}
```

liz (ML): Important: `compat_layers` isn't free. it implies we maintain a conversion shim (tokenizer/IO, small adapter) and test coverage. We should estimate 2-4 engineer-weeks per major model family. put that in onboarding cost sheet.

derek (CS): Addendum from support — we need a customer-visible migration doc template: timeline, potential behavior diffs, rollback steps, and an example curl with the pin header. customers want an easy toggle in Console to stay on the old model while they test.

sam (SRE): Ops constraints — if many customers pin older large models, capacity planning gets messy. ask: can we offer a paid dedicated pin pool or do soft eviction with warnings? Prefer explicit paid pool so capacity accounting is clean.

maria (PM): Good call. Propose two lanes: (1) free short-term pins (30 days) limited to N concurrent pins per org, auto-expire, and (2) paid long-term pins with SLA and dedicated capacity. Policy will be in the catalog doc.

jen (Sales): If we document the paid pin product clearly, customers will prefer it. include discount tiers for annual commitments.

ashok (Eng): For rollout: phase 0 = catalog metadata schema + console toggle; phase 1 = bench harness + onboarding checklist; phase 2 = paid pin infra + dedicated pool. estimate 6 sprints.

liz (ML): Can we bake in an A/B migration pattern for testing model replacements? runtime should support routing 5/95 split and store per-prompt annotations for automatic quality alerts.

maria (PM): Yes. Add rollout gates: (a) bench pass (b) no more than 1% quality regression on customer flagged prompts (c) automated rollback on >2% error spike during canary. These become hard launch criteria.

derek (CS): I'll draft the customer migration template and a sample support playbook. Canary-run checklist please.

ashok (Eng): I'll start a PR for the catalog schema and the minimal routing changes. tagging folks: @liz @sam for review.

canary-bot: new canary checked in: `canary/xyz-13b` passed warmup. details: https://ci/internal/2423

maria (PM): Next actions: Derek + Jen create customer comm + pricing spec by EOD Fri; Ashok + Liz put up schema PR and benchmark harness prototype by next Wed; Sam to sketch capacity model for paid pin pool. I'll consolidate into roadmap ticket after PRs land.

jen (Sales): flagged: two customers already asked for multi-month pins. I'll collect contract language examples and share.

ashok (Eng): FYI command to run the micro-bench locally:```bash
./bench/run.sh --model xyz-13b --seq 512 --iters 200
```

maria (PM): Thanks all. We'll reconvene in the product sync next Tue. :rocket:
